props.title: Tweet Drafts: Downstream-of-Product Signal
props.description: the downstream-of-product signal — builders building load-bearing infra on top of you

props.author: Draft 1a
props.text: forks are flattery. people building load-bearing infra on top of you without asking is the real signal.

props.author: Draft 1b
props.text: you've made it when someone benchmarks you academically and you find out after they shipped it ⭐

props.author: Draft 2a
props.text: same day: someone ships an ed25519-signed schema to verify our skills, someone preregisters an academic replication study of our sim. nobody asked us. that's the tell 🦈

props.author: Draft 2b
props.text: stars measure attention. forks measure curiosity. infrastructure built on top of you measures inevitability. different ladder.

props.author: Draft 3a
props.text: there's a moment where people stop asking you for features and start building load-bearing infra on top of you. signed skill schemas. replication studies. merchant catalogs on your rails. you don't request these. they happen to you once you're real ⭐🦈

props.author: Draft 3b
props.text: the ecosystem tell isn't forks. forks are cheap. it's when builders standardize you — sign your skills, benchmark your sim, treat your output as a wire format. that's when you stopped being a repo and became infrastructure.

props.author: Draft 4a
props.text: watched two things land the same day. someone shipped an ed25519-signed schema to verify our skills and called the output "the wire format." someone else preregistered a multi-replication academic study of our swarm sim — grok judge, the whole setup. neither asked permission. neither needed to. that's the phase shift nobody warns you about: you stop chasing adoption and become the thing other people build on. forks are downstream of curiosity. trust layers and benchmarks are downstream of product ⭐🦈

props.author: Draft 4b
props.text: the trap when builders start building on top of you: you celebrate the fork and miss the move. someone standardizes skill-trust before you do. someone defines the benchmark before you do. now your category has a spec you don't control. validation and threat are the same event here. when people build infra on your product you either curate the trust + verification layer or you wake up inside someone else's standard. own it early ⭐

props.author: Draft 5a
props.text: how do you know a product crossed from "interesting" to "infrastructure"? not the star count. you watch what people build on top of you without asking first 🦈

props.author: Draft 5b
props.text: forks are the most overrated metric in open source. they cost nothing. the one that matters: is anyone building load-bearing infra on top of you yet ⭐

props.title: Recommendation
props.message: Best: 4a — the two unprompted signals carry the whole thesis; specific, earned, lands on "downstream of product."
